jobs.description: Are you an engineering leader who has defined a bold strategy for your space and delivered on it? Have you built and led teams through transformation where the ambition grew faster than the headcount, and come out the other side with big results? Amazon Software Builder Experience (ASBX) is looking for a Software Development Manager to lead the team, product and engineering strategy, and delivery of transformative testing and verification solutions at agentic scale at Amazon. We are creating new AI systems that decide what to test, write the tests, explain what went wrong, and close the loop fast enough for an agent to self-correct without human intervention. As a Software Development Manager in ASBX, you will be a product and people leader for products across the Testing suite. You will define the strategy for how AI-powered testing capabilities mature from early adoption (10K+ monthly active users today) into the default way every team at Amazon validates software in the AI Development Life Cycle. You will own the product vision, the roadmap, the team, and the results. You are joining an experienced team that is already shipping. Your job is to force-multiply it: sharpen the strategy, raise the ambition, grow and support the team, and deliver at a pace that matches how fast the problem is moving. This role requires a leader who has done this before, not someone looking to learn it for the first time. Key job responsibilities - Defining and owning the product strategy for AI-driven testing at Amazon: what to build, in what sequence, and why that sequence wins. Your strategy must be defensible to senior leadership and ambitious enough to match the rate at which agents are changing how software gets written; - Hiring, growing, and leading a large engineering team through a period of rapid expansion and increasing scope; - Partnering with your SDE, PE, and PM colleagues to translate product direction into technical architecture, and holding both accountable to coherence; - Meeting with customers across Amazon to understand how they test today, where their testing breaks down, and what would make them trust AI-generated test evidence enough to ship on it; - Driving delivery execution at a pace that matches the domain. Capabilities in this space that ship six months late ship into a world that moved on; - Owning the product vision for your area. You partner with a product manager, but the vision, the conviction, and the hard prioritization calls are yours; - Deeply shaping the direction of TestSpaces, ensuring that the execution layer and the testing-judgment layer evolve as a coherent system rather than adjacent efforts; - Communicating strategy, progress, and risk to senior leadership clearly and without hedging. A day in the life You lead the team building AI testing capabilities already in daily use by tens of thousands of Amazon engineers, and you are pushing those capabilities from useful individual tools into a coherent testing system that operates across the development lifecycle. On a given day you might be: working with a PE on tech strategy; reviewing architecture and tech designs with your engineers; meeting with another Amazon team as your customer; reviewing Go-To-Market progress with our PM, or presenting your roadmap to ASBX leadership and defending the sequencing choices. Your customers are every builder at Amazon. Your immediate partners are your PE, your product manager, and the teams who own the testing platforms, deployment infrastructure, and AI coding tools that your work builds on and feeds into. The right product decisions in this space compound across the entire company. About the team Our group exists to make testing in the AI Development Life Cycle a solved problem rather than a growing liability. In the Testing org, our platforms execute millions of tests per day across every AWS region. Our AI systems make those platforms smarter: generating tests, diagnosing failures, measuring sufficiency, and helping builders ship with confidence. The Pipeline Test Fixer alone has surpassed 50,000 daily invocations and reduces median promotion-blocking time by 25%. TestSpaces is already validated at scale, with a sibling organization running 2 million AI-native end-to-end tests per month across 500+ production pipelines on our execution layer. The capabilities in our strategy range from production to proof-of-concept, and the person who leads this team will decide which of them become products and which get cut. You will thrive here if you have a track record of defining product strategy in ambiguous, fast-moving technical domains; if you have built and led high-performing engineering teams through periods of growth; and if you have the conviction to make hard calls on what to build, and what to stop building, when the landscape shifts under you.

You’ll learn how to manage complex projects, communicate clearly with stakeholders and turn data into action. Are you ready for work that moves you? Over time, you’ll be confident discussing trends and their impact. Who we serve. From large institutions to private wealth managers, you’ll see how we support a wide range of clients — and how their goals shape the way we work. What we offer. You’ll get to know our product range — funds, ETFs, tailored solutions — and learn how we match the right offering to the right need. For example, how we support advisors helping clients save for retirement versus those focused on growth. The tools we use. You’ll get hands-on with the platforms and software that keep our client work running — from relationship tracking to Aladdin, our proprietary tech for building and analysing portfolios. How to connect and communicate. You’ll pick up the skills that make strong sales and service work — from tailoring your message across markets to writing a clear, concise follow-up email that hits the right note. The rules we stick to. You’ll gain a solid understanding of the ethics and regulations that govern how we work — always putting clients first and acting with integrity. Examples of the work you’ll do as a Graduate Analyst: Meeting with clients: You might manage logistics and materials, take notes and follow up with answers — while also beginning to build your own relationships and network. Drive outreach : You could run a mini-campaign — for instance, inviting 50 advisors in Germany to a webinar for a new fund launch. Build strong pitch materials: You’ll help prep for client meetings with materials that turn data into a story — like charts, insights and investment ideas. Spot client trends: You might look at sales data to find out what’s gaining traction — e.g. “Which fund types are growing fastest in the UK?” — and share the insights with your team. Keeping ahead of trends is what keeps us moving forward. Expand your network : You’ll connect with peers across the industry through events, conferences and meetings — building your presence and shaping your own unique perspective. You’ll understand how products like ETFs work, why investors choose them, and what makes them tick — from broad exposure to thematic strategies like AI or Clean Energy. How to build better portfolios . You’ll help translate complex markets into practical guidance. What can help reduce risk? Where can clients find income? You’ll help answer questions like these. How new ideas become real products. You’ll follow the full lifecycle — from initial idea to design, regulation, naming, launch and sales strategy. For example, you might explore the opportunity for a “European Defence ETF” and help shape how it comes to market. How to manage complex projects. You’ll coordinate across legal, operations, compliance and more — learning to keep a multi-step process moving forward on time. How we take products to market. You’ll learn how to build messaging that lands, figure out who a product is for, and choose the right channels to reach them — whether that’s a research paper, a campaign, or a one-on-one conversation. Research that drives decisions. You’ll dig into trends and analyse data — for example, how similar funds have performed, or whether a gap in the market exists. You’ll learn how to turn research into real recommendations that move our clients forward. Creative thinking. You’ll work on ideas that push our industry forward. That might be designing an active fund that supports the transition to low-carbon economies — balancing big ideas with what’s actually possible. Examples of the work you’ll do as a Graduate Analyst: Support a product If something is in motion while you’re on rotation, you’ll help manage the timeline, work with key teams, and tick off the checklist that turns an idea into something people can invest in. Become a product expert. You’ll learn how specific investments work — and help explain them to colleagues and clients in simple, useful ways. Improve portfolios. You’ll use tools like Aladdin to analyse performance and suggest adjustments — or explore how market events are shaping portfolio decisions. Track the big picture. You’ll help us understand where the industry is going — like which funds are gaining interest and how we compare to others. Explore new product ideas. You might research whether there’s a demand for something like a Space Technology ETF — exploring the audience, competitive landscape, and market opportunity. Your recommendation, either way, will count. Write clear materials. You could draft the first version of a fund factsheet or internal briefing — helping to explain a product’s purpose and appeal in a way that makes sense to any reader. Who we’re looking for We’re looking for smart, curious people who are ready to learn, grow and bring energy to a client and product-focused environment. About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic's APAC go-to-market organisation is the fastest-growing part of our international business, spanning markets with distinct languages, cultures and buying styles. Today, enablement for the region is delivered by our global and EMEA teams. You will be the first enablement leader on the ground in APAC.
You will change that. As the first enablement leader based in APAC, you will own how the field across the region gets ready: onboarding, ongoing skill development, manager coaching support and launch readiness, for every GTM function, not just sales. You are the multiplier. You turn a rapidly scaling region into a field that is ready for the customer conversations in front of it, in the languages those conversations happen in.
This is a build role with a global spine. You inherit a working global and international enablement engine. Your job is to design for APAC as part of that engine, adapted and translated where it matters, delivered across APAC, feeding what you learn back into the international and global programme. Design, influence and translate, in both directions.
How we work: adults learn by doing, we build sessions around live activity: practice, reflection, real customer scenarios. The measure is not what was covered in the room. It is what changes a week later in how people think, decide and sell.
This takes creativity and a deep understanding of how adults learn, applied at unprecedented speed. The frontier moves quickly and the field is scaling fast. Much of the work is unlearning: helping experienced sellers let go of pre-AI habits, not just teaching new ones. AI is what makes this scalable. Infinite practice partners, personalised scenarios from real deals, feedback minutes after a call. You will use it that way, not to generate more content.
Key responsibilities
Stand up the APAC enablement rhythm: in-region onboarding cohorts, live practice-based sessions in APAC time zones, and a regional feedback loop into the global programme
Adapt the international portfolio for APAC, where enablement for several markets must be written and translated ahead of delivery rather than spoken and hoped for
Partner with regional GTM leaders to build a coaching standard that scales as the manager layer grows
Own launch readiness for the region. When a new model or product ships, the APAC field is certified and conversation-ready in the same week cycle as everyone else
Run practice-first sessions in the room: deal walkthroughs, role-plays, customer-conversation rehearsal. Practice and application over presentation
Minimum qualifications
Have 15+ years in GTM enablement, sales productivity or field roles, with several years leading enablement
Have built and led GTM enablement in APAC, with direct experience in more than one of the region's markets
Have influenced and shipped beyond your own region, from a global seat or a regional one: a programme adopted elsewhere, or a senior stakeholder outside your reporting line whose decision you changed
Personally design practice-first enablement and measure it by what the field does differently afterwards, not content shipped or attendance
Understand how adults learn and apply it at unprecedented speed. Much of the job is helping experienced sellers unlearn pre-AI habits, not just teaching new ones
Are creative with the craft. You use AI to give every seller personalised practice, real-deal scenarios and fast feedback, not to produce more content
Have owned a function with end-to-end accountability rather than orchestrated one
Have enabled a field across languages and cultures. You know what breaks when content built for English-first markets ships as-is
Operate as the region's first enablement leader: prioritising ruthlessly, borrowing leverage from global programmes, knowing when to adapt versus adopt
Work fluently with sales leaders as a peer: pipeline reviews, deal inspection and forecast conversations, not just training rooms
Strong candidates may also
Have held both a global and an APAC enablement role
Have run enablement delivered across APAC markets
Have built a regional enablement function from zero
Have carried a quota or led sellers earlier in their career
Have enablement experience in AI, developer platforms or technical products sold to both executives and builders
Have built manager or coaching programmes, not just individual-contributor enablement
Logistics
Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit
anthropic.com/careers
directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!

jobs.description: OVERVIEW The Workplace Experience team powers and connects the workday for all Perplexity employees across our global offices. We are hospitality and experience-driven at the core. We are made up of People people, meaning that we love supporting each other and all of the People in our workplace. We take on the good and the bad with optimism and with a positive, kind approach to solving problems, dealing with the obstacles handed to us, and proactively creating good around us. We think about each moment through the lens of our colleagues (our customers) so that we can create thoughtful and memorable experiences no matter what task we have at hand. As our Global Workplace Business Operations Lead, you will manage the business operations and cross-functional program delivery that enable our global Workplace Experience team to scale. In collaboration with the Head of Workplace Experience, you will set the operating framework for your areas, make decisions within agreed priorities and approval limits, and remain hands-on in delivering results. You will own the effectiveness of portfolio operating processes and internal project delivery. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own the Workplace operating framework: Lead annual and quarterly planning for your areas, translate team strategy into priorities and resource plans, and establish clear decision rights, delivery commitments and measures of success. Resolve sequencing and capacity trade-offs within agreed parameters and recommend when to add people, vendors or technology. - Lead internal capital-project delivery: Take accountability for integrated delivery plans across office openings, refreshes and other capital initiatives. Direct the work of external PMs within agreed scopes, align internal workstreams, resolve delivery issues and hold partners accountable for schedule, cost, quality and operational readiness. - Own portfolio controls and insight: Establish dependable lease administration, obligation tracking, space and occupancy information, and portfolio reporting. Set data and control standards, ensure actions have owners, and turn trends and risks into recommendations before deadlines or capacity constraints become problems. - Drive financial planning and performance: Own the processes and quality of operating and capital forecasts, commitments, actuals and variance analysis in partnership with Finance. Challenge assumptions, recommend corrective actions and investment trade-offs, and give the Head of Workplace Experience a reliable basis for budget and commitment decisions. - Set the systems and reporting roadmap: Own business requirements, governance and improvement priorities for workplace tools such as Envoy. Establish useful performance measures, improve data quality, and automate repeatable work while maintaining appropriate controls and keeping processes practical for the team. - Lead EHS program governance: Establish a risk-based plan, clear responsibilities and a review cadence with qualified vendors and internal teams. Drive follow-through on assessed obligations and remediation across offices and remote populations, maintain evidence of completion, and escalate material risks without substituting for specialist advice. - Set standards for delivery and handover: Own the development and use of project playbooks, planning processes and operational-readiness criteria. Bring together design standards and occupancy requirements, and ensure completed projects transfer to local operations with the documentation, training, vendor arrangements and issue ownership needed to run well. - Serve as a senior operating partner: Lead cross-functional operating and project reviews, surface decisions with clear recommendations, and represent your areas with internal and external partners. Drive resolution within your authority, escalate material changes with options, and build accountability without adding unnecessary layers. WHAT YOU BRING - Senior functional leadership: 8+ years in workplace business operations, corporate real estate, facilities programs or a closely related field, with increasing responsibility for complex, multi-site programs and their outcomes. You have operated with substantial autonomy, not only administered plans set by others. - Project and program management expertise: You are a project manager at the core. You are quick and agile, but methodical when it comes to planning for, organizing, tracking, and executing on a project in a way that keeps everything and everyone aligned and on task. - Relevant delivery depth: You have a record of delivering office buildouts, relocations or capital improvements as an internal owner, with accountability for scope, financial performance, schedules, change control and external delivery partners. - Strong financial and analytical judgment: You have experience driving forecasting and reporting processes, challenging assumptions and translating portfolio data into resource or investment recommendations; strong spreadsheet and analytical skills. - Experience building an operating framework: You have established planning, governance, performance measures and systems that helped a growing function deliver more predictably. You know when structure improves execution and when it becomes unnecessary process. - Leadership across organizational boundaries: You can secure commitments, challenge constructively and resolve competing priorities across teams and vendors. You communicate risks and recommendations credibly to senior leaders and know which decisions to make independently and which to escalate. - Hands-on ownership and sound judgment: You can move between portfolio-level trade-offs and project details, deliver through others without losing accountability, handle sensitive information responsibly, and maintain a kind, service-oriented approach under pressure. - Helpful, not required: International portfolio experience, workplace technology ownership, EHS program governance, or a relevant project-management credential.
